p: it came to pass: Christ witnesses by his going to death voluntarily, that he will make full satisfaction for the sin of Adam by his obedience.
Ye know that after two days: God himself and not man appoints the time that Christ should be crucified.

feast day: By the word "feast" is meant the whole feast of unleavened bread: the first and eighth day of which were so holy that they were not allowed to do any work on it, though the whole company of the Sanhedrin determined otherwise: And yet it came to pass through God's providence, that Christ suffered at that time, so that all the people of Israel might be witnesses of his everlasting sacrifice.

Now when Jesus was in Bethany: By this sudden work of a sinful woman, Christ helps the guests to understand about his death and burial which was near: the gracious result of which will bring life to all sinners who flee unto him. But Judas takes an occasion here to accomplish his wicked purpose and plan.
There came unto him a woman: For these things were done before Christ came to Jerusalem: and yet some think that the evangelists have two differing accounts.

box of very precious ointment: These boxes were of alabaster, which in ancient times men made hollow to put in ointments: for some write that alabaster keeps ointment without changing it in any way; Pliny, book 13, chap. 1.
disciples saw it: This is a figure of speech called synecdoche: for it is said that only Judas was moved at this; Joh 12:4.
waste: Unprofitable spending.
When Jesus understood it: We ought not to rashly condemn that which is not orderly done.
For ye have the poor always: Christ, who was once anointed in his own person, must always be anointed in the poor.
in that she hath poured this: In that she poured this ointment upon my body, she did it to bury me.

Now: Christ purposing to bring us into our country without delay and so, to pay the penalty of the law, truly fulfils the law, omitting the contrary tradition and custom of the Jews: and thus shows that all things will so come to pass by the ministry of men as governed by the secret plan of God.

the first day of the feast: This was the fourteenth day of the first month: now the first day of unleavened bread should have been the fifteenth, but because the evening of this day (which after the manner of the Romans was referred to the day before) belonged by the Jews' manner to the day following, therefore it is called the first day of unleavened bread.

sat down with the twelve: Because the Law appointed them to be wearing footwear, and to have their staffs in their hands, as though they were is haste, therefore it is to be gathered that they did not sit down when they ate the Passover, but stood, for normally when they went to eat they took off their shoes: therefore he speaks here in this place, not of the Passover, but of the supper which was celebrated after the Passover was solemnly done.

dippeth his hand with me in: That is to say, he whom I invited to come to my table, alluding in this to Ps 41:9, which is not to be understood as though just as the Lord spoke these words Judas had his hand in the dish (for that would have been an undoubted sign) but it refers to his tabling and eating with him.
which betrayed him: Who was thinking of nothing else but to betray him.
And as they were eating: Christ who will without delay fulfil the promises of the old covenant, institutes a new covenant with new signs.

blessed it: Mark says, "Had given thanks": and therefore blessing is not a consecrating with a conjuring type of murmuring and power of words: and yet the bread and the wine are changed, not in nature but in quality, for without doubt they become tokens of the body and blood of Christ, not of their own nature or force of words, but by Christ his institution, which must be recited and laid forth, that faith may find what to lay hold on, both in the word and in the elements.

this is my body: This is a figure of speech which is called metonymy: that is to say, the giving of one name for another: so he calls the bread his body, which is the sign and sacrament of his body: and yet nonetheless, it is a figurative and changed kind of speech meaning that the faithful do indeed receive Christ with all his gifts (though by a spiritual means) and become one with him.
all of it: Therefore they who took away the cup from the people, disobeyed the instruction of Christ.
For this is my blood of: That is, this cup or wine is my blood sacramentally, as in Geneva "Lu 22:20".
new testament: Or covenant, that is to say, by which the new league and covenant is made, for in the making of leagues they used the pouring of wine and shedding of blood.
an hymn: When they had made an end of their solemn singing, which some think was six Psalms, Ps 112:1 - 117:2.
Then saith Jesus unto them: Christ, here taking more care of his disciples than of himself, forewarns them of their falling away, and provides them with some comfort.

Then cometh Jesus with them unto: Christ having regard to the weakness of his disciples, leaves all the rest in safety, and takes with him but three to be witnesses of his anguish, and goes on purpose into the place where he would be betrayed.

very heavy: The word which he uses signifies great sorrow, and tremendous and deadly grief: this thing, as it indicates man's true nature, which shuns death as a thing that entered in against nature, shows that though Christ was void of sin, yet he sustained this horrible punishment, because he felt the wrath of God kindled against us for sins, which he revenged and punished in his person.

Then saith he unto them: Christ, a true man, who is about to suffer the punishment which we should have suffered for forsaking God, is forsaken by his own: he has a terrible conflict with the horror and fear of the curse of God: out of which he, since he escaped as a conqueror, causes us not to be afraid of death any more.
let this: Let it pass me, and not touch me.
cup pass from me: That is, which is at hand, and is offered and prepared for me: an idiom which the Hebrews use for the wrath of God, and the punishment he sends. See Geneva "Mt 20:22".
And he cometh unto the disciples: An example of the carelessness of man.
Rise: Christ offers himself willingly to be taken, that in so obeying willingly he might make satisfaction for the wilful fall of man.
from the chief priests and elders: Sent from the high Priests.
And Jesus said unto him: Christ is taken, that we might be delivered.
Friend: Christ reprehends Judas tauntingly, and rebukes him sharply, for he knew well enough why he came.
Our vocation must govern our zeal.
take the sword shall perish with: They take the sword to whom the Lord has not given it, that is to say, they who use the sword and are not called to it.
Thinkest thou that I cannot now: Christ was taken because he was willing to be taken.

But how then shall the scriptures: By this questioning he answers a sly objection, for they might have asked him why he did not in this his great extremity of danger call to his Father for aid: but to this objection he answers by this question.
And they that had laid hold: Christ being innocent is condemned by the high Priest for that wickedness of which we are guilty.
Caiaphas the high priest: From Annas to Caiaphas, before whom the multitude was assembled; Joh 18:13.

palace: The word used here properly denotes an open large room in the front of a house, as we see in kings' palaces and noblemen's houses: we call it a court, for it is open to the air, and by the use of synecdoche, is understood to mean the house itself.
what is it which these witness: How does it come to pass that these men witness against thee?
Hereafter shall ye see the Son: This word distinguishes his first coming from the latter.

on the right hand of power: Sitting with God in like and equal honour at the right hand of his power, that is, in greatest power: for the right hand signifies among the Hebrews that which is mighty and of great power.
clouds of heaven: Clouds of heaven; see above in Mt 24:30.

rent his clothes: This was a peculiar custom among the Jews: for so were they bound to do when they heard any Israelite blaspheme God, and it was a tradition of their talmud in the book of the magistrates, in the title, of the four kinds of death.

Now Peter: Peter by the wonderful providence of God, in being appointed to be a witness of all these things, is prepared to be an example of outstanding faithfulness through this experience of unbelief.
sat without in the palace: That is, outside the place where the bishop sat, but not outside of the house, for afterward he went from there into the porch.
curse and to swear: He swore and cursed himself.
